scope: 1959 SNU GSPA first intake, founding chronology, and dean/actor network

findings.claim: A near-contemporaneous first-decade overview by Hahn-Been Lee states that GSPA was operationally established in April 1959 and enrolled a first class of 100 MPA candidates: about 40 daytime recent graduates and about 60 self-financing evening students drawn from middle/top civilian bureaucracy, government corporations and the armed forces.
findings.provenance: Hahn-Been Lee, 'The Graduate School of Public Administration, Seoul National University: An Overview of its First Decade', KJPA 7(1), 1969, pp.14-16; SNU repository PDF.
findings.implication: Pass 135's bounded 80 first-graduate population must not be conflated with the initial intake. The research graph now needs separate intake-1959 and graduation-1961 populations, with attrition/non-completion left open.

findings.claim: The same overview dates the SNU-University of Minnesota-ICA support contract to February 1957, the first group of eleven mainly Law College faculty departures to Minnesota to August 1957, the first Minnesota adviser arrival to March 1958, and contract termination to June 1962.
findings.provenance: Hahn-Been Lee, KJPA 7(1), 1969, citing Lloyd M. Short, Terminal Report, June 1962.
findings.implication: The institutional founding event should be decomposed into pre-founding technical-assistance, faculty-training, adviser-arrival, legal-establishment, operational-opening, first-intake and later separation sub-events.

findings.claim: SNU GSPA's current official history records January 1959 establishment by Presidential Decree and March 1961 delivery of the first MPA degrees to 80 graduates.
findings.implication: January 1959 legal establishment, April 1959 operational opening/first intake, and March 1961 first graduation are distinct chronology nodes rather than a single founding date.

findings.claim: An official SNU GSPA brochure gives the institution date as 1959-01-13 and lists Shin Tae-hwan as first dean from 1959-04-10 to 1960-09-19, Lee Byeong-do as acting dean from 1960-09-20 to 1961-03-31, and Lee Yong-hui as dean from 1961-04-01 to 1962-02-10.
findings.implication: The founding/first-graduation period has a concrete senior governance chain that should be represented as actor nodes and linked to the relevant institutional sub-events, without inferring policy authorship.

findings.claim: The same official dean table records Kim Jong-han (1962-02-11 to 1966-10-31), Hahn-Been Lee (1966-11-01 to 1970-09-09), Cho Seok-jun as acting dean (1970-09-10 to 1970-11-25), Kim Yun-tae (1970-11-26 to 1972-11-25), Park Dong-seo (1972-11-26 to 1976-11-25), and Yu Hun (1976-11-26 to 1982-12-05).
findings.implication: This creates a reusable institutional leadership spine for later politician/bureaucrat-network research and helps distinguish founding-era actors from later institutional leadership.

findings.claim: The Academy of Korean Studies encyclopedia identifies Hahn-Been Lee (李漢彬, 1926-2004) as a career official and educator: Education Minister's secretary from 1948, Planning Office budget chief, Finance Ministry budget director, 11th administrative and political vice-minister, diplomat, later SNU GSPA professor/dean, and in 1979-1980 Deputy Prime Minister and Economic Planning Board minister.
findings.implication: Unlike purely academic founding actors, Hahn-Been Lee clearly crosses the politician/senior-state-actor threshold and merits an independent stable politician/bureaucrat node if not already present.

findings.claim: SNU's university-wide history separately describes GSPA as becoming independent in the 1961-1973 professional-graduate-school expansion period.
findings.implication: This corroborates that 1959 establishment and 1961 independence/separation are different institutional acts; the exact March 1961 instrument remains an archival target.

adversarial_checks: Do not equate the 100-person April 1959 intake with the 80 March 1961 graduates.
Do not infer that the difference of roughly 20 represents dropouts without individual enrollment/degree records.
Do not collapse January 1959 legal establishment and April 1959 operational opening into a contradiction; preserve both with event semantics.
Do not infer that all approximately 60 evening students were civil servants; Lee explicitly includes government corporations and armed forces.
Do not infer that all eleven August 1957 trainees later became GSPA faculty without the Minnesota/ICA roster.
Do not infer that a dean authored the Presidential Decree or admissions policy solely from office tenure.
Do not treat the later official brochure as a substitute for contemporaneous appointment orders for dean start/end dates when exact legal authority matters.
Do not classify Shin Tae-hwan, Lee Byeong-do, Lee Yong-hui or Kim Jong-han as political actors merely from GSPA deanship; test their public-office careers independently.
Do not infer that Hahn-Been Lee participated in the 1959 founding merely because he later served as dean; his verified state career and later GSPA tenure must be temporally separated.
Do not silently harmonize the current GSPA January establishment wording with Lee's April operational wording; model legal and operational sub-events.
